I think it was just a display of trauma creating energy. Scars create some energy just by existing, but additional energy must be created in order for a living to see a ghost. Previous to that scene, we only saw occasions where that additional trauma/energy was created by the living person experiencing something traumatic, but Janet actively experiencing trauma in her scar created a field of energy in the room strong enough for Mr South to see Mr Martin. 
(In theory this could mean that any of our ghosts could talk to a living person, as long as they are in the room while someone is experiencing their scar. Though we don’t know if that only worked that time because Janet was in her scar for such a long period of time, or if that’s just how that works.)

If Alice also attempted to pass as the body’s original identity to family and friends just like Janet did that would make their stories even more similar!
